Glycogen breakdown in muscle begins with glycogen phosphorylase cleaving α-1,4-glycosidic bonds to release glucose-1-phosphate. This occurs before any conversion to glucose-6-phosphate. Glucose is not the initial product because muscle lacks glucose-6-phosphatase, and glucose-1,6-diphosphate is not a primary product of glycogenolysis.  

Final answer: (B)
